author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Dozens of rescuers were called to Mount Lafayette on Saturday after a 62-year-old hiker was injured, according to WMUR.

The rescue began at about 3:30 p.m., the station reported. Mount Lafayette is one of the prominent peaks in Franconia Notch, an area that can require extended responses when hikers are hurt on steep or difficult terrain.

WMUR’s initial report did not identify the nature of the hiker’s injury or provide additional details about the person’s condition. It also did not report any other injuries connected to the incident.

The response highlights the coordination often required for mountain rescues in New Hampshire. Hikers can face changing weather, uneven footing and long distances from roads or medical access, making preparation and route awareness important even during day trips.
NorthEast News will update this report if authorities release additional information about the hiker or the rescue response.
dek: A 62-year-old hiker was rescued from Mount Lafayette Saturday after an injury prompted a coordinated response, WMUR reported.
headline: Dozens of rescuers help injured hiker off Mount Lafayette
